note: PROPOSED World at War style numbers for the Zombies mode (open for the user, see docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md). Round 1 sends a handful of slow zombies; health grows by 100 a round to round 9, then 10 percent a round; runners from round 3, sprinters from round 5. Points: 10 a hit, 60 a kill, 100 a headshot kill, 130 a melee kill, 10 a board.

rounds.note: Player scaling (2026-10-27): a round sends (countBase + countPerExtraPlayer x (players - 1)) x the round's fraction; the alive cap is maxAliveCurve x (1 + maxAlivePerExtraPlayer x (players - 1)), never over maxAlive (at most 600, the code's limit). Bots count as players; a host who sits out doesn't. A join or leave mid-round works both out again at once for the new count: the zombies already killed or alive stay counted, so the rest is the new total less those (never below 0), and a leave never ends the round on the spot.

playerDrops.note: A gun dropped with the drop key, or loose parts dropped from the parts inventory or the workbench, lie on the floor until the end of the round after the one they were dropped in (rounds; 0 = no round limit) or for seconds, whichever comes first. At most maxPartDrops part pickups on the map at once (past it a drop is refused, nothing is lost), each holding up to maxPartsPerDrop parts of one kind.

perks.name: Ironhide Cider
perks.blurb: Zombie hits do 40 percent of their damage.

perks.name: Second Wind
perks.blurb: When you go down, you get back up on your own after a few seconds (used up).

perks.name: Marksman Malt
perks.blurb: Headshots do 50 percent more damage; headshot kills pay 50 more points.

perks.name: Bloodroot Tonic
perks.blurb: Melee does double damage, and every melee hit heals you 30.

perks.name: Windfall Soda
perks.blurb: Your kills have a 6 percent chance to drop a power-up (up to 2 over the round's limit).

perks.name: Hammerhand Ale
perks.blurb: Rebuild barriers 2.5 times as fast, for double the board points.

perks.name: Salvage Stout
perks.blurb: Your kills drop parts twice as often; salvage piles give you a part more.

perks.name: Bulwark Brew
perks.blurb: An armour plate takes a whole zombie hit, then grows back 12 seconds later.

grenades.note: Every player carries this grenade in Zombies (Frag or Impact). At the start of every round each player's grenades are topped up to start + floor((round - 1) / roundsPerExtra): rounds 1-3: 1, 4-6: 2, 7-9: 3, 10-12: 4, and on up (no cap; developer's decision 2026-10-27). A spawn gets the same count.

box.note: The last part of each offer is free for all (2026-10-27): for the final freeFraction of offerSeconds or the last freeSeconds, whichever is longer, anyone can take the gun (the first take wins); before that only the buyer can. Taking it apart stays the buyer's. Both 0: buyer only.

slots.note: PROPOSED slot machines (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, Slot machines): a pull costs costBase + costPerRound a round after the first (at most costMax); the reels spin spinSeconds and a win shows showSeconds. A part you already hold dupePointsAt of loose pays pointsBack instead (0: always keep it; 0 since 2026-10-27: loose parts have no cap, bank as many as you like; pointsBack still pays the coin result). The odds by round are DropTables.json slotTiers. No pull pays nothing (2026-10-27): a blank (the skull, slotTiers 'nothing') pays a consolation part of the machine's own category, its rarity from consolation[bet level] (weights per rarity; not the round's table, so commons stay in late rounds; never rarer than the main roll's lowest part tier at that bet); it frees the machine at once, never resets the heat and doesn't count as a pity win. Heat: every pull without a pityTier-or-better part adds 1, every heatStep heat moves the part odds one rarity up (at most heatMaxSteps), such a part resets it. Bets (2026-10-26): the second key at a machine cycles its bet; a pull then costs the price x bets[level] and moves the part odds betSteps[level] rarities up on top of the heat (the blank and coin weights stay: no sure big win). maxNothing (at most that many nothing-results in a row) is unused since consolation parts: kept so it can come back. Every jackpotEvery-th round adds jackpotLegendary / jackpotWonder to the odds and puts the wonder symbol on the reels.

machines.note: PROPOSED per-category slot machines (2026-10-26; a map's slots entry with "category"): each only pays parts of its category, with the same odds table, heat, bets and jackpot rounds as the classic machine but its own heat. price is a multiple of the classic machine's price (to the nearest 10); melee: the blade (a whole melee build) is on its reels (default: the melee categories only; elsewhere a melee result pays a part of that tier).

casino.note: PROPOSED casino tables (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, Casino tables): bet points (only points: no money, no progression) at a map's tables. Each game's min / max bet (roulette: a player's total on one spin; a map's table may set its own); every bet is a whole number of betStep. Blackjack waits dealSeconds after the first bet for other seats, then each hand has turnSeconds to act (then it stands). Roulette takes chips for rouletteBetSeconds after the first one, then the wheel spins spinSeconds. High-low and dice wait actSeconds for you to act (then high-low cashes out, dice rolls). A result shows showSeconds. You play within useRange of a table; an unfinished hand is forfeit past leaveRange (or when you go down). High-low pays (1 - highLowEdge) / the guess's chance per correct guess, at most highLowMaxSteps guesses. A win of announceAt points or more over the bet is shown to everyone.

powerUps.note: World at War style power-ups (milestone 3; Infinite Ammo and the weights 2026-10-23; the points schedule 2026-10-26). A drop becomes due once the team has earned firstAt points (hits, kills, boards), and the next kill drops it; each later one is due a step later that grows x stepGrowth a drop (at most stepMax). dropChance is an extra flat chance per kill (0: off). At most maxPerRound a round; it floats for lifetime seconds (blinking for the last blinkSeconds). The timed ones (Insta-Kill, Double Points, Infinite Ammo) last their durations entry, or duration seconds. Max Ammo is the most common drop (about 38 percent).

ammoEffects.note: PROPOSED (milestone 3): what part flags do to zombies (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, Special ammo effects). One effect of each kind per shot or swing, never stacked.

bots.note: Co-op bots spend their own points like players (2026-10-26; ZombieBotsShop.cs): only when it's safe (the break, or no zombie within quietRange and nobody down), within shopRange of their post, keeping reserve points. Priorities: the power switch, perks in perkOrder (saving up for the next one it can reach), a better wall gun (wallBetter x the damage per second in hand), the slot upgrade, the box (boxSurplus spare), a door between rounds (one a break for the team), a slot pull (slotSurplus spare).

horde.note: The horde controller (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, Horde controller): level of detail (think every 1/2/4/8 ticks by distance), window queues, flanking round to other windows, surrounding, spreading over the players, reacting to gunfire, blasts, downs, power-ups and hurt neighbours, regrouping when blocked, shared flow fields.

limbs.note: Dismemberment (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, Dismemberment; Source/Game/ZombieLimbs.cs): each arm and leg has healthFraction of the zombie's health (at least healthMin) times its type's healthMult; a hit on a limb (damageShare of it) or a blast (blastShare, by each limb's distance) takes it off. One arm swipes weaker and slower, none bites; one leg limps; none crawls (slow, low reach, a prone-sized hit box, slow at windows). The pieces fly off as pooled gibs (goreCap pieces at most, goreSeconds each). types: walk, run, sprint (brutes and specials get their own when they exist; severs false ignores dismemberment).

crowd.note: The mass horde's crowd tier (docs/zombies/MASS-HORDE.md), only on maps whose zombies section has "crowd": zombies as particles that read a shared flow field (flowCell m cells, rebuilt every flowRefreshTicks, flowCellsPerTick of it a tick) every thinkMin-thinkMax ticks, walk at speed (+- speedSpread) and push apart (separationRadius, separationStrength, at most separationMax neighbours). Within promoteRange of a player the nearest become full zombies (promotePerTick a tick, at most individualCap at once); a healthy one further than demoteRange for demoteSeconds goes back to the crowd (demotePerTick a tick).

climb.note: The bell siege (docs/zombies/ZOMBIES-MODE.md, The bell: a siege up the tower; Source/Game/ZombiesClimb.cs): ringing the Cathedral's bell starts a 75 s survival challenge in the belfry. The horde outside leaves the windows for the tower's north face, piles up against it in a living pyramid (layers layerHeight apart, columns columnSpacing apart, each layer layerShrink columns narrower than the one under it, the bottom baseRows layers two deep, at most layers high) and climbs over it and up the bare wall (one in climbEvery goes straight up from the start); a shot zombie lets go and falls, dazed fallStun seconds where it lands, and the bodies above a shot one slide down. The siege adds extraZombies + extraPerRound a round (at most extraMax) to the round. Surviving pays every player standing rewardPoints + rewardPerRound a round (at most rewardMax), rewardParts loose parts rolled as if it were rewardRoundBonus rounds later (rarer), and drops rewardPowerUp on the belfry.
